lines:
Follow-up from task 143 (number 142) part 4, rescoped 2026-09-26 after review. The original scope was a segmented or map-reduce summary; the decision is to do the fitting reduction instead - choose the summary cut from the window, and let the existing drop ladder terminate in a lossy commit. Segmented/map-reduce is out of scope here, recorded only as a future quality option for the day a small window becomes a first-class target.

REACHABILITY. The recorded 32k run was the 64k-floor bug (0.8 x 32,000 = 25,600 never armed until 142,887 tokens), but the class survives commit 3173c99 in three ways that are not bugs:
1. A single oversized step. The token trigger is evaluated once per model request, at context preparation, so the surface can jump past W between two preparations. Nothing local stops it: the acting gate is a byte bound, MAXIMUM_PROVIDER_REQUEST_BYTES = 32 MiB (pipeline.rs:93), roughly 250x a 32k-token window, so a pasted log, a large file read or several images pass it. Measured: a 1920x1080 image costs about 968 prompt tokens, and up to MAX_REQUEST_IMAGES = 16 / MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BYTES = 24 MiB may attach newest-first in one turn (about 15k tokens), which with F about 12.3k exceeds a 32k window on its own.
2. A declared window that shrinks under existing history. Adopting a newer workflow revision can change the model/provider snapshot and the compaction target; continue, fork and portable import bring long history into a possibly smaller window. History does not shrink when the window does.
3. A provider that enforces less than declared, or a window typed smaller than the real one. Only the provider's rejection reveals it, and the reaction is Trigger::ContextOverflow after a failed turn.

WHAT HAPPENS TODAY. The summary call sends the whole shadowed span in one request (measured 156,336 input tokens / 540 KB on the local qwen run). When it cannot fit, the recovery ladder prunes tool results and then shrink_summary (surface.rs:271) drops the oldest eligible unit one at a time, bounded by SUMMARY_SHRINK_RETRIES = 2 (mod.rs:422): at most three attempts and at most two drops, then it gives up, warns "Context is still above the configured pressure threshold after the permitted reductions", and leaves the selection unchanged. ProviderError::InputBoundExceeded or a provider overflow routes to Trigger::ContextOverflow (retain 0, one attempt, pruning), so the only guaranteed lossy reduction runs only after something has already failed.

WORK
1. Size the cut instead of discovering the mismatch by trial and error: fixed_tokens and the per-unit token prices are known, so keep the newest whole units whose tokens fit W - fixed - directive and spend one call.
2. Make the ladder terminate in a fitting commit rather than a warning: when even the minimum summary prompt cannot fit, skip the summary and commit the lossy reduction the ContextOverflow shape already produces (retain 0 plus pruning), so the context always ends below its declared window.
3. Keep whole units as the drop granularity. Cutting inside a message would split tool call/result pairs and break the balanced-boundary invariant the checkpoint relies on; shrink_summary already protects the base user message and the directive.
4. State the consequence in evidence rather than hiding it: the checkpoint then summarises only the newest part of the shadowed span and the oldest part is dropped without a summary. Lossy, bounded, one call - the same "compacts badly rather than ignoring its window" rule the derived floor already follows.

ACCEPTANCE. A run whose prefix exceeds its declared window ends with a committed reduction that fits, never with an unchanged selection plus a warning; the summary cut is chosen from the measured window, not by retrying the provider; strict-shrink, balanced-boundary, exactly-once lifecycle and durable-replay guarantees still hold; no regression for large windows (test1_3 stays at 64,192 uncached and 9/9 conformance).

BOUNDARIES. Owns the summary call shape and the terminal lossy reduction. Task 137 (id 138) owns which units may be shadowed; the trigger (0.80) and the budget arithmetic are settled and out of scope. Segmented/map-reduce summarisation is explicitly out of scope.

AMENDED 2026-09-26 (commit 1a0f8e6). Every compaction budget is now a share of the effective window, so the two constants quoted above are gone. The floor plan at 32k with fixed about 12,300 is 8% of the window - 2,621 tokens, R 1,620 / S 1,001 - instead of a fixed 2,512, and there is no 8,000 summary cap: the intended summary length is min(38.2% of the replacement budget, the model's declared output), so a 1M window with no declared output reservation plans R 154,342 / S 95,402, and a model declaring 8,000 output tokens bounds itself at S 8,000 (R 241,744). Work item 1 therefore means: keep the newest whole units whose tokens fit W - fixed - directive, where the directive size comes from the policy's own summary share rather than from a constant. The authoritative model is the specification aworkit.workflow_worker.context_compaction_budget.

data.title: Guarantee a fitting reduction when the prefix no longer fits the window
